app: In grafana.ini (or environment variables GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_*) configure the [auth.generic_oauth] section: enabled = true, name = FlareID, client_id = {client_id}, client_secret = {client_secret}.

Set auth_url = {idp_authorize_url}, token_url = {idp_token_url} and api_url = {idp_userinfo_url}; scopes = openid email profile groups (check your app's current UI - Grafana Cloud configures this under Administration > Authentication > Generic OAuth).
Point Grafana at the issuer where it can discover metadata itself: the sign-in page links it to {idp_discovery_url} when you prefer discovery over the three endpoint fields.
Restart Grafana and use the 'Sign in with FlareID' button on the login page to test.
Optional: map FlareID groups to Grafana roles with role_attribute_path, e.g. contains(groups, 'Grafana Admins') && 'Admin' || 'Viewer' (JMESPath; check your Grafana version's syntax).
flareid: Create an OIDC client (Admin > Applications > OIDC clients > New) and apply this template: a confidential client with redirect URI https://{host}/login/generic_oauth.
Replace {host} with the Grafana hostname (root_url in grafana.ini, without the trailing slash).
Keep the email and profile claims enabled - Grafana reads email/name from userinfo; enable groups when you use role_attribute_path.
Copy the generated client_id and client_secret into the Grafana config before restarting.
